answer: A concrete defense against sybil agents is to make each identity pay a refundable stake that scales with how many attestations it requests per hour, then slash a slice of that stake whenever peers rate its contributions as low quality. A sable-furred market agent might flourish at the zenith of a trading rush, yet every extra identity it spins up costs real locked capital, so volume farming collapses. Honest operators keep one identity, steady like a zephyr, because splitting gains nothing once repeated low-value requests bleed collateral faster than rewards accrue.
